newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals lifted by short covering.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals lifted by short covering.

text.p: Short covering helped lift precious metals prices on Monday and simultaneously lightened the dark mood which last week's disappointing close had cast on the market, dealers said.
"There has just been short covering so far. I haven't seen any fresh buying," one market analyst said.
Gold was fixed at $379.75 per ounce versus $378.15 on Friday afternoon and a close of $378.70/$379.20.
"Some hope was generated with large buying of $390 calls (call options) on Friday. Buying out-of-the-money calls has often been the forerunner of a decent move," one dealer said.
It was unclear whether the option purchase was a new position or shorts seeking upside protection, the dealer said.
A call option gives its holder the right but not the obligation to buy a commodity at a given price, known as the strike price, at a set date.
Often they are used speculatively, aimed at making a profit, but more recently the options market has been used more defensively to protect contract prices.
An "out-of-the-money" option would be one in which the strike price was noticeably higher or lower than the underlying market price at the time the contract was made.
Dealer said the gold market could be looking for $380.25-$381.00 as a target on Monday. "After the $381, we could see some buy stops," one dealer said.
However gold's potential was in the hands of the miners who were rumoured to be lining up sell orders to be released as soon as the price tried to rise.
"If they do, gold won't go. If they don't it's got a chance," one dealer said, adding that a sustained rise was more likely to be "nibbled at" than attract fresh buying quickly.
Dealers noted that a fairly quiet trading day was expected.
France and Belgium were closed to mark Armistice Day and although the New York markets would be trading, the United States would be partially closed for Veterans' Day.
Silver was also expected to try the upside with a target of $4.88 per ounce, about eight cents above the Friday close.
At 1045 GMT it was indicated at $4.84/$4.86. "It is not so obviously inhibited by producer selling as gold. If it can make $4.88, it has the potential for more," one dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were both steady and firmer at $383.00/$384.00 and $116.75/$117.75, up $1.05 and $0.75 respectively.
